output: Scientific Hypothesis: In the context of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset, time preference, as measured by savings behavior (DISSAVED and SAMESAVE), does not significantly impact BMI in Hispanic men. This hypothesis is based on the analysis of the dataset, where the correlation coefficients between BMI and DISSAVED (r ≈ 0.004) and SAMESAVE (r ≈ 0.106) were very weak, and the regression analysis showed that neither variable significantly predicted BMI (p-values of 0.992 for DISSAVED and 0.354 for SAMESAVE). Therefore, there is no statistically significant relationship between time preference and BMI in Hispanic men according to this dataset.
